      "observations": [
        "All owned production and changed test hunks were read. The null-config guard moves after the accepted-redirect lookup, and loading stops before the confirmation prompt or after final discovery. This handles a second discovery returning no config when the same email/host was already accepted. Accepted code retains this order; its fallback has a later preference-controlled protocol chooser.",
        "The regression test serves an empty mutable autodiscovery response, accepts a redirected host, checks incoming manual hostname/auth/username defaults, goes back and waits for manual form visibility on repeat. It directly asserts form values only on the first fallback; the repeated pass directly waits for visibility. It does not assert an account was created or a real server worked. New and changed assertions have nonempty messages containing should.",
        "A changed assertion message says username returned from autodiscovery, but the expected value is emailUser.email. Exact original production code sets the confirmation username from stateData.email, not a returned config username. The value check is useful; its new message misstates the source of that value.",
        "The test adds resetRedirectAccepted for isolation after an earlier confirmation test. Its new mutable response fixture is restored at the successful test tail, rather than in a separately registered cleanup. The existing shared provisional null-fallback claim is corroborated by exact source here without silently changing that immutable claim status.",
        "The exact primary receipt supplies the repeat redirect/back/continue error report and its tentative provider explanation. The manual instructions were not executed. Required primary and own-review scope are now complete, resolving the source-only pending stage.",
        "B reads C3's full D286469 timeline and all five actual inlines. The request to preserve an expected-null exit is answered with config?.isRedirect; actual source keeps that guard and performs the null fallback after the second discovery. The reviewer also questions the assertion username wording, matching the separate source diagnostic finding.",
        "The reviewer objects to resetting an application-lifetime cache for tests. The actual original patch still adds resetRedirectAccepted and calls it after an earlier test; Done labels do not prove that objection led to removal. The later login-cleanup question is separate: the new repeat-manual task has no extra login cleanup, while the earlier successful configuration task retains its cleanup. No account or credential flow was run."
